claims.text: ledger.default_db_path(), which honours DAEDALUS_SPINE_DB. NOT picker.resolve_spine_db_path(), which ignores that variable (picker.py:438 vs ledger.py:157 -- a live divergence Codex owns; it is not fixed here).

claims.text: Lives HERE rather than in ledger.py, and ledger.py imports it back, for one structural reason: ledger.py is a CONSUMER of this module (its rows carry a trace and project to statements), so the dependency has to run envelope <- ledger or it is a cycle.
claims.why: No import or usage of ledger.py is shown in this chunk.

claims.text: sort_keys makes two dicts built in different insertion orders produce byte-identical text; separators strips the whitespace a pretty-printer would vary; ensure_ascii pins the bytes so a digest does not depend on the reader's encoding.
claims.why: The function calls json.dumps with sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True, matching the claim.

claims.text: Mirrors memstore._body_sha's discipline: one place, one answer to 'what bytes did we hash?'.
claims.why: No reference to memstore or _body_sha is present in this chunk.

claims.text: sha256 over canonical_json -- stable across insertion order.
claims.why: The function computes hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(obj).encode('ascii')).hexdigest(), exactly as claimed.

claims.text: The file bus carries the trace inside the record for bridge hops (which is the standing rule -- no side channels), but a plain subprocess has no record to carry it in, so the environment is the only honest channel left.
claims.why: No code implementing bridge hops or subprocess propagation is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Read at current_trace_id time rather than cached at import, so a parent that binds after import still propagates.
claims.why: The current_trace_id function body is not fully shown; no reference to os.environ is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Sortable by eye, unique in practice.
claims.why: The returned string includes a timestamp and a uuid fragment, making it sortable and practically unique.

claims.text: Shape tr-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSS>-<8 hex>, matching the house style already in loop.LoopDriver.run_id.
claims.why: The function returns f'{_TRACE_PREFIX}{time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}' which matches the described shape.

claims.text: The stamp is for humans reading a directory listing; the uuid fragment is what makes it unique -- a collision needs two mints inside the same SECOND that also agree on 32 random bits.
claims.why: The timestamp provides second granularity and the uuid fragment adds 32 bits of randomness, making collision extremely unlikely.

claims.text: The tr- prefix exists so a partial id is still recognisable in a grep hit.
claims.why: The prefix is defined as 'tr-' and used in the returned string.

claims.text: The trace id in scope, or None.
